research_concepts: derived possession records (initiator, play type, points)
teammate action sequencing and its effect on play outcomes
methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR raise PNR points per possession, relative to matched PNR possessions without that preceding action?
Are the DRIVE and PNR labels, and the PPP outcome, reliable enough to support a sequencing test?
Is the PPP outcome derived from the same labeling pipeline that defines the predictor, creating label dependence?
How should sequence-level exposure counts and sample size be handled for PNR outcomes?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned zero records, so no earlier study by this project on this question, on teammate DRIVE sequencing, or on play-type label reliability is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a DRIVE before a PNR raises PNR PPP.
Whether the derived play-type labels are accurate, and how often DRIVE or PNR tags are misassigned.
Any effect size, direction, or variance for sequencing effects.
Whether the question has already been answered outside this project.
own_inferences: The play-by-play is a plausible source for sequencing, since it records action types, players, clock, and score in order, so a DRIVE-to-PNR sequence within a possession can be reconstructed.

The derived possession graph is built from the same play-by-play, so the PNR and DRIVE tags and the PPP outcome may share upstream classification errors, and the test may partly measure the labeling pipeline.
The predictor is a sequence condition within a small subset of possessions, so exposure per team, player, or season may be sparse, and per-season estimates may be noisy.
A positive association could be produced by the defense's response, by shot-quality confounding, or by the lineup and matchup context in which DRIVEs and PNRs co-occur, not by the sequence itself.
uncertainties: Exact frequency of teammate DRIVE-then-PNR sequences in the data is unknown.
Accuracy of the play-type classifier in the derived graph has not been audited in any retrieved record.
Whether the 2025-26 playoff data is complete at the time of testing is unknown (partial before 2026-06-21).
The retrieval tool may have had no records simply because no earlier work was stored, not because none exists.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no historical finding, failed approach, or prior result was available to alter the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone.

blocking_constraints.text: PPP and the DRIVE/PNR tags come from the same derived play-type graph, so the outcome and predictor share a labeling pipeline that must be audited before a contrast can be read as a basketball effect.
No reliability estimate for the play-type labels is available; misclassified DRIVE or PNR tags would bias the contrast toward or away from zero.
Teammate DRIVE-then-PNR sequences may be rare per team-season, limiting precision for individual players or lineups.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was returned by retrieve_history, so no prior study is relied on and the question's status (answered or not) cannot be determined from this setting.

risks.text: PPP and the predictor both come from the derived play-type records, so a labeling artifact could create or hide the effect.
Misassigned DRIVE or PNR tags in the play-by-play-derived graph would attenuate or distort the estimate.
Defensive scheme, matchup quality, shot-clock state, score margin, lineup, and player quality may drive both DRIVE-then-PNR occurrence and PNR PPP.
Sequences may be sparse for many player pairs, leaving unstable per-pair estimates.
The effect size is unknown; the number of qualifying sequences per season may be too small to detect a modest PPP difference.
Scanning many action pairs (DRIVE, SPOT_UP, HANDOFF, etc.) before PNR would inflate false positives if all are tested.
If placebo sequences (e.g., DRIVE following PNR) show similar effects, the result may reflect general possession quality rather than sequencing.
Possession-level features taken from the full possession, including its outcome, would leak the result into the predictor.
Play-type definitions, tracking, and offensive style may change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooling seasons may mix different regimes.

design.estimand: Within-possession difference in mean PNR PPP between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE (same possession, prior action) and matched PNR possessions without that preceding action, conditional on covariates listed under controls.
design.unit: PNR possession (ball-handler-initiated pick-and-roll possession), nested within team-game and player pair.
design.sample: Development: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs. Confirmation: 2025-26 regular season only (complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs until complete (2026-06-21) and exclude partial 2025-26 regular-season data before 2026-04-13.
design.power: Before analysis, compute the number of qualifying DRIVE-then-PNR sequences per season and the minimum detectable PPP difference at 80% power and alpha 0.05 using the development sample; if the minimum detectable effect is larger than plausible, report the question as underpowered rather than rejected.
design.controls: Ball handler and screener identity or skill proxies, defensive matchup and partial possession measures, shot-clock and score margin, period and clock, lineup and substitution-interval context, starter status, and season fixed effects. Use only information available before the PNR begins to avoid lookahead. Include random effects for player pair and team-game.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo sequences: teammate DRIVE following a PNR, and teammate SPOT_UP or HANDOFF preceding a PNR; the DRIVE effect should exceed these. (b) Label audit: manually verify a random sample of DRIVE and PNR tags against raw play-by-play, and report misclassification rates before interpreting the contrast. (c) Re-run the outcome with a PPP definition built independently of the DRIVE tag.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary contrast (DRIVE before PNR, PPP). Treat other action pairs as exploratory and correct for them (e.g., Holm) if reported as findings.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary contrast is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero in the development sample, the sign replicates in the 2025-26 regular-season confirmation sample, the effect exceeds the placebo contrasts, and the label audit shows acceptable misclassification. Rejected if the CI is tight around zero with adequate power. Otherwise report uncertain. Report artifact if the effect disappears after using an independently derived PPP or after the label correction.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, and defensive matchup files as stored in the derived play-type graph on 2026-06-14; record the exact graph build version and freeze it before analysis; use 2025-26 regular season only in the complete-data window.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
